bull.b: Exceptional revenue growth demonstrates strong demand for Nebius's AI infrastructure and rapid customer adoption. Expanding scale can improve infrastructure utilization, reinforce market positioning, and create a larger recurring revenue base over the next several quarters.

High customer prepayments reduce the amount of capital Nebius must fund internally while improving visibility into capacity demand. This funding model can support faster expansion, strengthen liquidity, and lessen the cash burden of building AI infrastructure at scale.

Vertical integration across hardware, infrastructure and software gives Nebius greater control over performance, utilization and cost. Its managed inference platform can add higher-margin software economics and deepen customer dependence on an integrated AI stack.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated consistent profitability from core operations, despite strong top-line growth. Persistent operating losses can constrain reinvestment, increase dependence on external funding, and make earnings quality more vulnerable to execution setbacks.

Negative free cash flow indicates that expansion is currently absorbing substantial cash beyond operating inflows. If large outlays persist, Nebius may need continued financing or customer prepayments, increasing execution pressure and reducing flexibility during slower growth.

The step-up in leverage raises financial risk as Nebius funds a capital-intensive infrastructure build-out. More debt can increase obligations and restrict future capital allocation, leaving less balance-sheet flexibility if deployment takes longer or returns arrive later.
